subject: physics
topic: Motion: speed, velocity, acceleration and equations of motion

kept.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes speed from velocity?
options: Speed is a vector quantity while velocity is a scalar quantity
Both speed and velocity are scalar quantities
Speed is a scalar quantity while velocity is a vector quantity
Both speed and velocity are vector quantities
kept.explanation: Speed only tells how fast an object moves (magnitude only), so it is a scalar. Velocity includes both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. This is the standard physics definition.
kept.pidgin: Speed na just how fast something dey move, e no get direction, so na scalar. Velocity get both how fast and the direction, so na vector quantity.

kept.q: An okada (motorcycle) starts from rest and accelerates uniformly, reaching a velocity of 18 m/s after 6 seconds. Calculate the distance it covers during this time.
kept.explanation: Since motion is uniformly accelerated from rest, average velocity = (u+v)/2 = (0+18)/2 = 9 m/s. Distance = average velocity x time = 9 x 6 = 54 m.
kept.pidgin: Since e start from rest and dey accelerate evenly, average velocity = (0+18)/2 = 9 m/s. Distance = 9 x 6 = 54 m.

kept.q: A driver travels the first half of a journey from Benin to Asaba at a steady speed of 40 km/h and the second half at a steady speed of 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
kept.explanation: For equal distances at different speeds, average speed = (2 x v1 x v2)/(v1+v2), not the simple average. So average speed = (2 x 40 x 60)/(40+60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.
kept.pidgin: Since na equal distance for both parts, you no go just add the two speeds divide by 2. Correct formula na (2 x v1 x v2)/(v1+v2) = (2x40x60)/100 = 48 km/h.

kept.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2 and ignoring air resistance, find the total time taken for the ball to return to the point where it was thrown.
kept.explanation: Time to reach the highest point is u/g = 20/10 = 2 s. By symmetry of motion under gravity, the time to fall back equals the time to rise, so total time = 2 x 2 s = 4 s.
kept.pidgin: Time wey e go take reach the highest point na u/g = 20/10 = 2 s. Because the up and down motion dey symmetric, total time wey e go take come back = 2 x 2 = 4 s.
